mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate increases by more than 0.25% over the next month, higher discount rates reduce the present value of expected corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > (current value + 0.25%) in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the trigger period (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS increase < 0.25% in practice.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in PAYEMS (labor market activity) above the 12-month moving average coincides with rising consumer confidence and corporate hiring, which precedes S&P 500 gains over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average in the current month
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 60 days after the trigger, or PAYEMS does not cross the moving average in observed data.

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (industrial production) grows at a rate exceeding 2% month-over-month for two consecutive months, it signals robust economic momentum that drives positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST growth rate > 2% in month t and t+1
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative or non-significant during the two-month high-growth window (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) below its 50-week moving average for three consecutive months predicts supply-side weakness, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 50-week moving average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or statistically significant during the contraction period (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE above their respective 5-day averages create a dual inflation-plus-tightening signal that produces negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5-day moving average AND UNRATE > 5-day moving average in the same month, for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Dual inflation and rate hike environment
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or not significantly different from zero during the trigger period (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 3% for three consecutive months, it indicates weakening labor market pressures and supports a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as investors anticipate lower wage growth risks.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or not statistically significant during the low-unemployment period (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp spike in GDPC1 (GDP) quarter-on-quarter exceeding 2% followed by a rise in CPIAUCSL (inflation) above 3% suggests demand outpaces supply, predicting positive S&P 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 QoQ > 2% AND CPIAUCSL > 3% in the same quarter
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive or are insignificant during the identified imbalance quarter (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales) falls for two consecutive months below its 12-month average, it signals softening demand which precedes S&P 60-day declines.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-month moving average for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not negative or show a significant upward trend during the softening period (p < 0.05).
